ITEM.PTXT: The "GOA" collision safety body has been adopted, pursuing world top-level occupant protection performance in its class that meets not only Japanese safety standards and European safety standards but also the stricter targets set independently by Toyota. Furthermore, safety has been pursued from various aspects, such as by adopting a "head impact reduction structure" and a "brake pedal retraction reduction structure".

As a further evolution of the collision safety body "GOA", an "omnidirectional compatibility body structure" has been adopted, which pursues compatibility in collisions between vehicles of different weights and heights. By conducting frontal and side collision tests using 2t class passenger vehicles, collision safety performance that simulates accidents in the market has been pursued in terms of securing cabin space.

GOA stands for Global Outstanding Assessment, meaning a safety assessment pursuing world top level in its class. Cleared the full-lap frontal collision (55km/h), side collision (55km/h) and 40% lap offset frontal collision (64km/h) tests.
Full-lap Frontal Collision (50km/h) and Side Collision (50km/h)
40% Lap Offset Frontal Collision (56km/h)
Compared within the same displacement class.

Based on a monocoque structure, the arrangement and joint structure of each member have been optimized, and by straightening the main frame members and actively adopting high-tensile steel sheets, a lightweight, highly rigid body with little vibration and noise has been achieved.

High rust prevention performance has been ensured by extensively adopting anti-corrosion steel sheets and applying a lightweight undercoating with excellent chipping resistance to areas frequently hit by water and gravel, such as the inside of the wheel houses and both sides of the front floor.
Sound insulation technology has been fully applied to each part of the body, resulting in a body with excellent sound insulation.

A "pedestrian injury reduction body", which takes into consideration reducing injury to a pedestrian's head, etc. in the event of a collision with a pedestrian, has been adopted, and various impact absorbing structures have been provided at the front of the body.

An impact safety body (GOA) has been adopted that effectively absorbs and disperses collision energy through crushable front and rear body sections and highly rigid cabin sections, minimizing cabin deformation.

An all-direction compatibility body structure has been adopted. By using a structure that minimizes cabin deformation in frontal and side collisions, collision safety performance simulating real-world accidents is pursued.

Based on computer collision simulations and numerous actual vehicle tests, a rational body structure has been adopted that effectively absorbs and disperses collision energy not only in frontal and side collisions but also in offset frontal collisions in which only one side of the vehicle receives the impact.

A rational body structure has been adopted that minimizes cabin deformation while reducing the impact on occupants, by means of a framework from the front to the underbody that effectively absorbs and disperses the energy of a frontal collision and a strong cabin framework.

The front door inner reinforcement has been strengthened, creating a structure that efficiently disperses the collision load by effectively transmitting energy from the front side members to the roof, door belt line and rocker sections.
The front side members and crash boxes use high-tensile steel sheet, creating a structure that efficiently disperses the energy of a collision from the front.
An under member has been provided, creating a structure that efficiently disperses the energy from the radiator support.
A moment cancel member has been provided, creating a structure that efficiently disperses the collision load from the front side members.
A dash cross member has been provided, creating a structure that effectively disperses the collision load from the front side members to the belt line and roof sections.

A front side member rear No.1 reinforcement has been provided, ensuring the strength of the tunnel section and creating a structure that efficiently disperses the collision load from the front side members.

Around the door openings, high-strength framework members including reinforcements have been optimally arranged, creating a rational body structure that effectively absorbs and disperses the energy of a side collision.

High-tensile steel sheet with optimized strength distribution is used for the center body pillar outer reinforcement, rocker outer reinforcement and rocker inner panel, creating a structure that minimizes cabin deformation.
The roof section has a roof reinforcement, creating a structure that effectively transmits collision energy to the side opposite the collision.

The rocker section has bulkheads provided in the rocker cross section, creating a structure that efficiently transmits and disperses collision energy input from the lower part of the center pillar, etc. to each cross member.

In the doors, the door side impact protection beams are arranged so that their lower ends overlap each pillar, creating a structure that efficiently absorbs and disperses collision energy. In addition, door strength has been ensured by optimally arranging the reinforcements at the belt line.
Energy absorbers for impact absorption have been provided inside the front door trim, creating a structure that reduces the impact on occupants in a collision.

A rear seatback hinge bracket and wheel house reinforcement have been provided on the interior side of the rear end of the rocker section, creating a structure that efficiently absorbs and disperses collision energy from the rear door side impact protection beam via the wheel house to the cross member and rear seatback frame.
A "head impact protection structure" has been adopted to reduce the impact when an occupant's head, etc. strikes the pillars or roof side sections due to rebound in a collision.
The impact-absorbing garnishes with integrally molded ribs collapse, reducing the impact on the occupant's head.

A "brake pedal retraction reduction structure", which minimizes the rearward movement of the brake pedal by moving the brake pedal downward in a frontal collision, has been adopted to reduce the impact on the driver's lower limbs.

When the brake booster is pushed in by the rearward movement of the engine, etc. in a collision, the clip (bolt) securing the brake pedal support to the instrument panel reinforcement separates from the brake pedal support, and the brake pedal support moves rearward and downward along the guide plate. As a result, the brake pedal pad moves forward and downward.

A "pedestrian injury reduction body", designed to reduce injury to pedestrians in the event of a collision with a pedestrian, has been adopted. Impact absorbing structures are used around the cowl panel and hood panel, creating a body structure that reduces the impact on a pedestrian's head, etc.

The hood panel has an inner panel shape (longitudinal frame structure) that readily transmits impact in the longitudinal direction, reducing the impact on the head, etc. in a collision with a pedestrian. In addition, a dent reinforcement has been provided at the hood lock reinforcement to create a collision energy absorbing structure and to ensure sufficient stroke in a collision with a pedestrian. The mounting position of the hood striker has been revised to ensure energy absorbing space for the hood.

An open cross-section structure has been adopted for the cowl, and the front wall of the cowl louver has a cantilever structure, increasing the energy absorption efficiency in the expected head impact direction and reducing injury values. In addition, at the wiper pivots, an energy absorbing space is provided between the wipers and the cowl top outer front panel, and the pivots move downward in a collision, reducing the impact on a pedestrian's head.

A foam bead energy absorber has been provided in front of the front bumper reinforcement and a resin engine under center cover below the radiator support, creating a structure that prevents a pedestrian from being drawn under the vehicle in a collision and reduces the impact on the lower limbs.

PARA.TITLE: Body Sound Absorbing and Insulating Materials

ITEM.PTXT: Various silencers are placed in appropriate locations to minimize transmitted noise from the engine, tires, etc., providing excellent sound insulation.

A significant improvement in quietness has been achieved by adopting a 3-layer dash panel insulator with an olefin sheet sandwiched between felt layers and a dash panel outer insulator made of laminated nonwoven fabrics of different densities, as well as by reducing the size of the heater pipe passage holes and improving the seal with the column hole cover.
A damping sheet is provided on the interior side of the cowl top panel, reducing noise transmitted from the engine room.
Asphalt sheets and spray-on damping material are effectively arranged on the floor panel, achieving both high sound insulation and weight reduction.

Foam material for blocking cross sections and resin-molded foam material are optimally provided in each part of the body, and service holes are closed with sealer, etc., minimizing noise transmitted through the pillars, etc.

PARA.TITLE: Sound Absorbing and Insulating Structure (Engine Room Area)

ITEM.PTXT: A hood insulator is provided under the hood panel. In addition, a 2-layer structure with an air layer between the hood panel and hood insulator suppresses noise transmitted from the engine room.
A nonwoven fabric cowl insulator is provided on the cowl top outer front panel, reducing noise transmitted from the engine room.
Fender side covers that seal the gap between the front fender panels and the body are provided, suppressing the entry of road noise from the tires and reducing wind noise caused by air flowing in.

The dash panel area has a dash cross member connecting the left and right front side members, a cowl to brace connecting the cowl and floor tunnel, and a tunnel reinforcement. This reduces longitudinal vibration of the dash area and vertical swinging vibration of the cowl caused by vibration of the front side members, minimizing engine booming noise and road noise.

PARA.TITLE: Sound Absorbing and Insulating Structure (Cabin Area)

ITEM.PTXT: Front fender side panel protectors are provided to seal the gap between the front fender panels and the body. This limits the entry of road noise from the tires and reduces wind noise caused by air flowing in.
Sound absorbing material is provided on the fender liners to absorb road noise and ensure quietness.

The door opening trim of the front and rear doors adopts a full-circumference 2-layer seal structure (A-A cross section), ensuring sound insulation performance. In addition, an upper seal is provided at the joint between the rear door window division bar and the rear window upper frame.
The door closing sound has been improved by providing damping material on the inside of the door outside panel.
Rocker protectors are provided on the standard grade and side mudguards on other grades, reducing the noise of sand thrown up by the tires striking the underside of the rocker area (chipping noise).
By providing rear wheel house liners, high-frequency road noise and the noise of sand thrown up by the tires striking the back of the wheel house (chipping noise) have been reduced.
In the rear area, the arrangement and joints of the various frame members have been optimized to suppress inward collapse deformation of the pillars and ensure high driving stability.

In the rear area, body torsional rigidity has been improved by forming a continuous closed cross section in a ring from the back door opening upper frame to the roof side outer panel and rear floor cross member No. No.2.
Rigidity of the back door opening has been ensured by forming a continuous closed cross section.
The body lower back panel reinforcement has a closed cross-section structure and is joined to the left and right rear floor side members to improve body torsional rigidity.
By reinforcing the rear floor side members, vertical displacement of the rear floor side members is suppressed and body rigidity is ensured.

In the floor panel and rocker areas, movement of the body frame has been suppressed and high quietness ensured by providing rocker inner bulkheads, straightening rear floor cross member No. No.1, and ensuring high joint rigidity between the floor side members and floor.
High quietness has been ensured by optimizing the panel rigidity and bead arrangement of the floor pan and tuning panel resonance.
A front suspension member brace has been provided on the lower surface of the front suspension member to ensure the longitudinal rigidity of the front suspension member.

For the radiator support, a structure in which the radiator support and cooling unit move back together in a light collision (radiator support retraction structure) has been adopted, reducing damage to the cooling unit and the repair cost of large parts.
The crash boxes have a structure that effectively absorbs collision energy from the front bumper reinforcement, reducing damage to the body frame.
The front bumper reinforcement and radiator support (frame section) use a bolt-on mounting structure to improve serviceability.
The rear bumper arms use a bolt-on structure to improve serviceability.

A body lower back panel reinforcement has been provided for the lower back panel. This allows only the body lower back panel reinforcement to be replaced after a light collision, reducing repair costs.

In the rear underbody, rigidity has been improved by straightening the rear floor side members and providing reinforcement members, and by ensuring rigidity at the joint with rear floor cross member No. No.2, inward collapse of the rear floor side members against impacts from diagonally behind is suppressed, reducing damage to the body frame.

Excellent aerodynamic performance has been achieved through flush surfaces on all parts of the upper body, engine under covers and other parts on the underbody that control the airflow under the floor, and a flat underfloor, ensuring a high level of handling stability and straight-line stability at high speeds.
A rear spoiler has been provided at the rear end of the roof panel, with a design matched to the flow from the roof panel, to straighten the airflow and reduce driving resistance.
The front fender liners have a tunnel shape that guides the airflow under the vehicle to the brake calipers & rotors, improving brake fade resistance.

A recessed shape has been provided on the surface of the fender liner close to the front side of the tire to straighten the airflow in front of the tire at high speeds, improving the steering response.
By reducing the step between the windshield glass and roof, the airflow has been made smoother and appearance has been improved.

Taking into account the airflow between the hood panel and windshield glass, the cowl louver has a raised shape and the wiper arms are optimally arranged so that wind does not directly hit the wiper blades, reducing wind noise.

PARA.TITLE: Fuel Economy Improvement Structure for A/C Operation

ITEM.PTXT: By providing a hot air recirculation prevention shutter in the cowl top ventilator louver and introducing outside air directly, the temperature of the air introduced into the A/C unit is lowered, improving fuel economy when the A/C is operating in traffic congestion, etc.

A hot air recirculation prevention shutter has been provided between the front bumper and condenser (around the radiator support) so that heat in the engine room does not flow around from the sides of the vehicle to the front of the condenser. This suppresses the inflow of hot air to the condenser and reduces the compressor power consumption.
A towing hook has been provided for recovery when the vehicle is stuck. Vehicles of the same class can be towed.
Vehicles heavier than this vehicle cannot be towed. Attempting to tow a vehicle heavier than this vehicle may adversely affect the drivetrain or damage the towing hook or vehicle body.

Large parts such as the front bumper and door trim have dismantlability improvement marks indicating points that help make removal easier. This improves the efficiency of dismantling recyclable parts and also shows users the efforts made toward recycling.
